transcript.content: Hello. I am Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, my wife has been pushing me to talk to someone for a while. What finally made me agree to come in is... I just don't care about the things that used to keep me balanced. I used to do sailing races, volunteer at the historical society on Saturdays, tinker in my woodshop. But lately, all of that just feels like chores I keep putting off. I just don't have any interest in them anymore.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Well, it's been a little over a year now. It started right after this scaffold accident we had at work... we were going through a big business readjustment at the time. Yeah, it's been going on ever since then.
Have you ever experienced a similar period of feeling this way at any point in your life before this past year?

No, I haven't. I've always been a pretty active guy, keeping busy with my hobbies and work projects. So this feeling of just... not caring about any of it, it's completely new to me. I've never really dealt with anything like this before the accident.
Beyond the loss of interest in your hobbies, have you noticed any significant changes in your sleep patterns since this started?

Yeah, I have. Getting to sleep isn't usually the problem—most nights I can get to bed at a reasonable hour. But I end up waking up around two or three in the morning, and my mind goes right back to that job site. After that... I'm just lying there, listening for every little sound instead of getting any real rest.
When you wake up in the middle of the night and your mind goes back to the job site, do you feel as if you are actually reliving the accident or seeing it happen again in your mind?

Yeah, I do. It's not just at night, either. Out of nowhere, I'll just see that scaffold dropping in my head. It's as clear as a photo. It happens a lot if I hear a metal clank or, you know, a backup alarm on a truck. When it happens, for a few minutes, it's really hard to stay focused on whatever meeting or conversation I'm actually in. It just kind of takes over.
Looking back, did these intrusive thoughts and the loss of interest in your hobbies start immediately after the accident, or did they only begin to develop several months later?

Pretty much right away. It didn't take months to start. This has all been going on since the scaffold accident... which happened during our business readjustment phase. So, it's been a little over a year now that I've been dealing with it.
